questions.text: What should a tenant over the limit get back?
questions.evidence: The goal names 429 and Retry-After, but test/webhooks.test.ts expects 503 for every refused webhook.

options.label: 429 with Retry-After
options.consequence: Senders back off on their own; the 503 test changes for this case.

options.label: 503 as today
options.consequence: No test changes, but senders retry at once and the limit does not hold.

recommendation.why: It is what the goal says, and the standard answer for a rate limit.

safeDefault.why: A status code is cheap to change later.

questions.text: Do webhooks already queued before the limit count towards it?
questions.evidence: src/lib/queue.ts retries failed webhooks, and the task does not say whether a retry is a new request.

options.label: Retries count
options.consequence: A tenant with many failures hits the limit sooner.

options.label: Retries do not count
options.consequence: The limiter needs to know which requests are retries.

recommendation.why: A retry is the same webhook, and counting it punishes a tenant for an outage.

questions.text: Where does the per-tenant limit come from when a tenant has none set?
questions.evidence: src/config.ts has no rate limit key, and criterion 3 says the limit comes from config.

options.label: One default in config
options.consequence: Every tenant without its own value gets the same limit.

options.label: No limit
options.consequence: Tenants without a value are never limited.

options.label: Refuse to start
options.consequence: A missing value stops the service at boot.

recommendation.why: It keeps every tenant limited and is one value to change.

safeDefault.why: A default is easy to raise or remove.

assumed.text: The window is a sliding window of 60 seconds.
assumed.why: The goal says a window and names no shape; 60 seconds is easy to change in config.

assumed.text: Retry-After is given in whole seconds.
assumed.why: Seconds are the common form, and every client parses them.

proofs.why: A test can send one webhook over the limit and read the status and header.
The same test can send for a second tenant.
The limit is read through loadConfig(), so a missing key fails the typecheck.
